sentences.text: This animal possessed a long neck, long legs, and long arms ending in sharp grasping claws.
Its skull measured approximately 262 mm in length, which was less than half the length of its 600 mm neck.
Unlike later relatives, Harpymimus retained teeth in its lower jaw, featuring at least ten to eleven cylindrical teeth per side separated by interdental plates.
Researchers believe it used a beak on its upper jaw combined with these lower jaw teeth to grasp and hold food, rather than for cutting or piercing.
Harpymimus is one of only two known ornithomimosaurs that retained teeth, representing a primitive trait for the group.
The type specimen's skull is virtually complete but badly crushed, hiding some anatomical details.
A Soviet-Mongolian expedition discovered a Harpymimus skeleton in the Gobi Desert in 1981.
Rinchen Barsbold and Altangerel Perle named and described the species in 1984.
The genus name Harpymimus means "Harpy mimic" and references the Harpy of Greek mythology, while the species name okladnikovi honors the Soviet archaeologist Alexey Pavlovich Okladnikov.
Only one fossil occurrence of Harpymimus has been recorded in the Paleobiology Database.
Harpymimus belongs to the family Deinocheiridae.
A 2020 phylogenetic analysis classified Harpymimus as a basal deinocheirid.
Research suggests Harpymimus is more derived than Pelecanimimus but basal to the clade containing Garudimimus and Ornithomimidae.
Harpymimus fossils were found in the Mid-Late Albian Shinekhudag Formation in the Eastern Gobi Province of Mongolia.
Harpymimus lived during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 130 to 125 million years ago.
Harpymimus lived during the Albian stage, between 110.1 and 100.5 million years ago.
According to Kobayashi and Barsbold, Harpymimus is more derived than Pelecanimimus polyodon.
The analysis suggests that ornithomimosaurians later migrated to North America during or before the end of the Cretaceous.
